verdicts.strongest_argument: The CFO change is published in this capture, dated, and two months old. The appointment of Jonathan Collins was announced on 2026-06-29 and appears in the stored body docs/4f5b168d5df0737fa55ae98ce2a74c43b91e324c.txt at the 2026-06-29T11:03:17Z entry, with the 08-06 8-K at 2026-08-06T11:03:16Z in the same document, and the Form 3, Form 4 and the items 5.02/7.01/9.01 8-K are all in filings.json. A CFO start date, a base salary and a senior VP's phased retirement are exactly the facts an 8-K exists to publish, and the market had nine weeks with them. What is left is a behavioural heuristic - a new CFO's first print is the moment to rebase guidance or take a writedown - which is generic, applies to every CFO transition at every company, carries no size, and is unsupported by any dated source in the capture. It is also a claim about the shape of a possible disclosure rather than about the quarter, so its sign is indeterminate: a rebase can as easily reset the bar low and be bought. The corroboration is weaker than presented: a 13D/A accepted on 2026-08-03 is a holder's report of a completed change, its body is not stored, no holder is named and no stake size is given, and the coincidence with a start date is a coincidence of a five-business-day window. Note also that the 07-22 8-K item 5.07 the finding elsewhere relies on is itself the public record of the meeting outcome, so the sequence it describes was fully assembled on EDGAR.

verdicts.strongest_argument: A proxy contest is the single most heavily published corporate event there is, and this capture proves it: the activist's public demand for a director's resignation is in the stored body at 2026-07-01T23:50:18Z, the company's FOR-all-nine recommendation citing ISS support is at 2026-07-07T19:13:01Z, and the DEFA14A supplements of 07-09 and 07-13, the 8-K item 5.07 of 07-22 and the 13D/A of 08-03 are all in filings.json (docs/4f5b168d5df0737fa55ae98ce2a74c43b91e324c.txt, admissible snapshots per clean-view). Proxy solicitation material is mailed to every holder by law and ISS recommendations are distributed to the entire institutional base - there is no plausible sense in which a resolved July proxy fight is unpriced information in September. The finding's own claim that 'nothing in the capture reports the vote outcome' is answered by the filing it cites in the same sentence: an 8-K item 5.07 is the vote outcome. The residual - that a shareholder base which just voted on the strategy will read this print differently - is a statement about how the reaction might be shaped, not about a fact the market lacks, and it has no size. And the closing argument, that a 14.6% twenty-session decline 'is not what a market pricing an activist-supported turnaround looks like', is the baseline's own run_up_20d field used as evidence against itself: that decline is the pricing.
